source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 4, 4. Ταῦτα πεΠόνθασι πολιορκούμενοί τε καὶ ἀπαγόμενοι. λέγοις δ ἂν καὶ ὡς >λιμὸν ὑπέμειναν οὐκ ἄρτου, οὐχ ὓδατος< κατὰ τὸ προφητικόν, >ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἀκοῦσαι λόγον κυρίου<. διὸ νεογνῶν αὐτῶν προφητεύει.
pass_a_gloss: [Pass A] These things they have suffered both being besieged and being led away. And you would also say that “they endured a famine not of bread, not of water” according to the prophetic word, “but of hearing a word of the Lord.” For which reason he prophesies of them as newborns.
pass_b_english: These things they have suffered both being besieged and being led away. And you would also say that “they endured a famine not of bread, not of water” according to the prophetic word, “but of hearing a word of the Lord.” For which reason he prophesies of them as newborns.

choices.why: Origen allegorizes God’s word as sword at Lam 4:9.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Origen’s Greek Lamentations fragments. Sense checked against Klostermann GCS III. Modern English not copied. OET = no previous English translation.
